hint.text:
1. Proper nouns need capital letters.
2. Capital letters are needed at the start of a sentence.
3. Capital letters are needed at the start of speech.
hint.sound: Proper nouns need capital letters. Capital letters are needed at the start of a sentence. Capital letters are needed at the start of speech.

instruction.text: Find the words in the sentence below that need a capital letter.

atoms.a: Ethan said, it’s really nice to meet you!
atoms.b: ((ethan)) said, “((it’s)) really nice to meet you!”

instruction.text: Rewrite the speech with the correct words capitalised.

atoms.b: ((Ethan)) said, “((++It’s)) really nice to meet you!”

instruction.text: Find the words in the sentence below that need a capital letter.

atoms.a: Could you pass me the salt? asked Jennifer.
atoms.b: “((could)) you pass me the salt?” asked ((jennifer)).

instruction.text: Rewrite the speech with the correct words capitalised.

atoms.b: “((Could)) you pass me the salt?” asked ((Jennifer)).

instruction.text: Find the words in the sentence below that need a capital letter.

atoms.a: I went to Paris last month. It was amazing! Exclaimed Simon.
atoms.b: “((i)) went to ((paris)) last month. ((it)) was amazing!” exclaimed ((simon)).

instruction.text: Rewrite the speech with the correct words capitalised.

atoms.b: “((I)) went to ((Paris)) last month. ((It)) was amazing!” exclaimed ((Simon)).

instruction.text: Find the words in the sentence below that need a capital letter.

atoms.a: My German friend said, your British accent is very strong.
atoms.b: ((my)) ((german)) friend said, “((your)) ((british)) accent is very strong.”

instruction.text: Rewrite the speech with the correct words capitalised.

atoms.b: ((My)) ((German)) friend said, “((Your)) ((British)) accent is very strong.”
